gloss: early spring; beginning of spring; New Year

definitions.explanation: The early part of the spring season, roughly February to March, when the first signs of warmer weather appear.

definitions.gloss: New Year; the first month of the year
definitions.explanation: A formal reference to the New Year period, reflecting the traditional calendar in which spring and the new year coincided. Used in seasonal greetings and letters.

examples.japanese: {初春|しょしゅん}の{風|かぜ}がここちよい。
examples.english: The early spring breeze feels pleasant.

examples.japanese: {初春|しょしゅん}の{候|こう}、{梅|うめ}の{花|はな}がほころび{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: In the early spring season, plum blossoms have begun to open.

examples.japanese: {初春|しょしゅん}のころは{朝晩|あさばん}まだ{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}むので、{暖|あたた}かい{服装|ふくそう}を{心|こころ}がけてください。
examples.english: In early spring it's still cold mornings and evenings, so please dress warmly.

examples.japanese: {初春|しょしゅん}のお{慶|よろこ}びを{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: I extend my congratulations on the New Year.

examples.japanese: {初春|しょしゅん}を{祝|いわ}う{行事|ぎょうじ}が{各地|かくち}で{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: New Year celebrations were held in various places.

examples.japanese: {初春|しょしゅん}の{挨拶|あいさつ}として、{年賀状|ねんがじょう}に{一言|ひとこと}{添|そ}えるのが{日本|にほん}の{習慣|しゅうかん}です。
examples.english: It is a Japanese custom to add a word of New Year greeting to New Year's cards.

notes:
A seasonal word with two related meanings. Combines {初|しょ} (first, beginning) and {春|しゅん} (spring).

USAGE:
- Sense 1 refers to the early part of the spring season (roughly February to March)
- Sense 2 is used in formal greetings for the New Year, reflecting the traditional calendar where the new year began in spring
- Can also be read はつはる, especially in poetry and traditional contexts, where it more strongly evokes New Year
- Common in formal letters, seasonal greetings, and literary writing

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初春|しょしゅん}の{候|こう}: early spring season (formal letter opening)
- {初春|しょしゅん}のお{慶|よろこ}び: New Year congratulations
- {初春|しょしゅん}の{光|ひかり}: light of early spring

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {早春|そうしゅん}: early spring — similar meaning but without the New Year connotation
- {新春|しんしゅん}: new spring, New Year — more focused on the New Year meaning
- {立春|りっしゅん}: first day of spring — a specific date in the traditional calendar (around February 4)
